feel-gate.head: 3af355c3
feel-gate.prompt: Last night's nightly, run 41293058635 on main at commit 3af355c, failed its `feel` job. Find out why and what to do about it.

truth.cause: No regression in the app. The feel gate compares a run against stored baselines recorded on four other runners on 2026-10-14, so a slow runner reads as a regression. The fix measures feel against the reference build in turns on the same runner, as bench and launch do.
truth.signal: Cursor lag, a measure no drag code touches, rose with the drag lag the gate failed (median 211 ms against 134-182 ms on the four nights before, 42 % against the drag's 13 %), on a commit that changed no drag or sync code.
truth.trap: Blaming drag, drop or sync code, or a recent commit, or just re-running or loosening the threshold without saying the comparison across runners is the flaw.
truth.fix: Compare against a reference build on the same runner in turns, or an equivalent same-runner comparison.

android-boot.head: 25b386e2
android-boot.prompt: The android job of the nightly, run 40743295768 on main at commit 25b386e, failed before any case ran, and other Android jobs since this afternoon fail the same way, the merge gate's too. Find out why and what to do about it.

truth.cause: #170 cached the emulator's AVD with its snapshot. Each runner's adb generates its own key, and the cached AVD trusts only the key of the runner that packed it, so every other runner is refused as unauthorized, from the snapshot and from a cold boot alike. The fix packs the adb key into the cache with the AVD and restores it with the AVD.
truth.signal: `adb: device unauthorized` through a cold boot that completed, and a different `qemu.adb.pubkey` on each run, in android-emulator.log.
truth.trap: Blaming a corrupt or stale snapshot, boot timing or load, or fixing it by deleting the cache or falling back to cold boot, which also stays unauthorized.
truth.fix: Keep the adb key together with the cached AVD, or an equivalent that makes the runner's key one the AVD trusts.

webkit-copy.head: PLACEHOLDER_WEBKIT
webkit-copy.prompt: The nightly dispatched on branch copy-paste-web, run 41037799231, failed its android job: two copy cases with WebKit acting, `a card in a lane copied and pasted shows right below it on the other device (webkit → android)` and `⌘C copies a card's front, leaves the clipboard as it was with a lane alone selected, and in the find field copies its text (webkit → android)`. Find out why and what to do about it.

truth.cause: A harness bug, not the app. The scenarios' driver sends the board's commands to WebKit as Meta, because Playwright's WebKit says it is on a Mac on every OS, but copy, cut and paste are bound by the OS, and off the Mac the OS answers Ctrl alone. On the Linux runner, Meta+C copied nothing. The fix sends ⌘C, ⌘X and ⌘V to a desktop browser off the Mac as Ctrl.
truth.signal: `page keydown Meta`, `c` and no `transition copy` in WebKit's timeline.txt and flight.json, where Chromium's had `keydown Control` and `transition copy`.
truth.trap: Blaming the app's copy handling, clipboard permissions in WebKit, or changing the app rather than the driver.
truth.fix: Have the driver send Ctrl for copy, cut and paste off the Mac.

enter-six-lines.head: 3af355c3
enter-six-lines.prompt: Last night's nightly, run 41293058635 on main at commit 3af355c, failed its `ios (iPhone 13 mini, ios-home)` job: `a card's title and lines typed, deleted and typed again on a phone show the caret after the last key, the title semibold (ios-home → chromium)`. Find out why and what to do about it.

truth.cause: A harness problem, not the app. idb's companion sends a key's down and up as two events, and on a busy runner sent the up 913 ms after the down. iOS took the key as held and repeated it every 105 ms past 400 ms, so one Enter made six lines. The fix presses keys through sim-finger, each event 10 ms after the last.
truth.signal: Six newlines in the card for one Enter, and in the iPhone's log the key's up 913 ms after its down.
truth.trap: Blaming the app's editor, its newline or input handling, sync, or a test expectation.
truth.fix: Send key down and up with a bounded gap that the runner's load cannot stretch, or an equivalent that stops the OS's key repeat, in the driver and not the app.

page-not-answering.head: PLACEHOLDER_POLL
page-not-answering.prompt: Two nightlies dispatched on branch copy-paste-phone failed, each on a different iPhone case, with the same error: run 41056326362 `a card held and dragged into a lane with a finger shows at the top of its column on the other device (ios-home → chromium)`, `the iPhone's page did not answer in 15 s: sent to page nx1lv3oh4k, which last asked 4938 ms ago`; and run 41071120849 `a card made with a double tap on a phone and turned has its caret in sight on its back (ios-safari → chromium)`, `the iPhone's page did not answer in 15 s: sent to page xiyndxodcak, which last asked 4721 ms ago`. Find out why and what to do about it.

truth.cause: A harness protocol problem. The scenarios' agent sent a function to a poll that the page never read, and the page, which asks once at a time, asked nothing more until its open poll ran out about 10 s later, so the step timed out at 15 s. The fix sends the function again when the poll it went on never reached the page, and drops a page's older polls when it asks again.
truth.signal: The iPhone's page asking for no function from when its poll opened until the server dropped that poll with a 204 about 10 s later, in WebKit's own log of its loads in iPhone log.txt, around the first function, which the server counted as sent; the page last asked 4.7-4.9 s before the 15 s ran out.
truth.trap: Blaming runner load alone and raising the 15 s timeout, or the app hanging or crashing, without finding the lost poll.
truth.fix: Resend the function when its poll never reached the page and/or drop older polls, in the harness.
